title: Two seasons at the Piping Rock with Tommy Lyman
summary: Williams worked two seasons at the Piping Rock under Tommy Lyman, with headliners such as the Boswell Sisters, and notes Lyman wrote Kansas City Torch.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: And he used to come around and you know, push, what the hell you call it, I don't know. Tommy Harmon, who was with me. Oh man, he used to come around and tell them the clubs and you know, do a few numbers and they'd show him some tips. And I think he used to go in Royal and Canal and I was running. I was running. He comes down against me. I was with him sitting. We worked at the Piper Rock, two seasons. We had Martin Downey, Luther Guard. You know that guy, Lyman, he's talking about?

Yeah, but not much. Fair enough. We had four of them. We'd go back next season for the racing season. And we had Sophie Tuggett, Joey Lewis, and Connie Boswell. Now you know he must be a good entertainer to play those places. I was with him, oh I made some money with that guy. Boswell's sister. Huh? Boswell's sister. Yeah.
Well who was the, I think starting him out was Bill Coker. Did you know Bill Coker?

Well he was a famous newspaper man, either a sports writer or something, but he was originator of, I mean he got the Boswell's sister started I think, I don't know. Connie and the, what was it, two sisters? Connie was the crippled one. The crippled one, yeah.
Well Vett is still living, huh? No, they're all gone, no they're gone. One of them, one of them is alive. Yeah, there's a guy, there's a guy in Metry that keeps rights to all the time.
They broke up, you know, Connie went by herself for one.
Oh I know, but he was asking about the other one being alive. I don't know who.
Yeah, that is the one that's alive. Now who wrote the Kansas City Torch? You know that, Tony?

Tommy Lyman wrote that, I have a copy of it. When the gang was all gone once around the town looking for friends and company. We know it. Oh, excuse me Tony. No, I said we know it. I didn't say nothing about you except we know it. I thought you were going to do a duet. Yeah, I just was thinking that, you know, I heard that song. He wrote that, he was a very good entertainer. Yeah.
And he was smart. I mean he let somebody make him remarks and he turned around and make him look that small.
